title: POC scoping: cost modeling with Orion Dynamics
header:
Date: 2026-11-22
Time: 15:00 - 15:48 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Recorded via Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Orion Head of ML), Lena Moore (Orion Infra), Diego Ramos (Orion CPO)
summary: POC scoping focused on cost modeling and unit economics for a retrieval/assistant workload. Discussed throughput targets, per-token estimates across model variants, batching and KV/prefix caching knobs, quantization options, benchmark plan and a 2-week pilot timeline. Action: Redwood to send cost spreadsheet and benchmark runbook; Orion to provide sample traffic profile and dataset for test window.
topics: Per-token cost estimates and batching/caching knobs
Timeline and next steps for POC
action_items: Jordan Miles - Send detailed cost spreadsheet with per-token model profiles and assumptions - due 2026-11-25
Priya Shah - Draft benchmark runbook + instance/region recommendations - due 2026-11-24
Samir Patel - Share 7-day sample traffic trace + representative prompts (anonymized) - due 2026-11-24
Lena Moore - Provide network/VPC constraints and security contacts for Private deployment discussion - due 2026-11-26
next_steps: Redwood to deliver cost model spreadsheet and benchmark runbook (link in follow-up email)
Schedule 48-hour benchmark window w/ Orion's sample traffic (propose dates 2026-11-29 to 2026-12-01)
Orion to confirm success criteria and budget cap for pilot (weekly sync next Tue)
Schedule security deep-dive if Private/VPC is required (SE + security specialist)
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Jordan from Redwood Inference, with Priya from our SE team. quick roll call?
[00:08] Samir: yeah Samir here, head of ML at Orion. Lena and Diego are on.
[00:13] Lena: hi all
[00:15] Diego: afternoon
[00:28] Jordan: great. the goal today is to scope a POC for cost modeling — understand your workload, define success criteria, and plan a benchmark run. we want to map per-token estimates and batching/caching knobs to your budget.
[00:45] Samir: high level — we run an assistant on customer support logs, roughly 120 QPS peak, average 40 QPS sustained. prompts average 1.2k input tokens and generation about 150 tokens. important: 95th p99 latency target around 700 ms for hosted API, and we'd like cost to be sub $0.003 per inference on average otherwise exec will balk.
[01:15] Priya: okay that's helpful. curious if that 120 peak is bursts or steady?
[01:19] Samir: bursts, like 2-3 minute spikes during day.
[01:24] Priya: cool. so for sizing we'll run a model matrix: larger open models vs quantized int8 variants. batching helps with throughput but can increase tail latency — we'll show tradeoffs. also prefix / KV cache can cut generation tokens when prompts repeat, any idea on repeat rate?
[01:42] Samir: about 30% prefix reuse on our flows, we have a lot of templated prompts.
[01:50] Jordan: nice, that moves the needle. for per-token modeling we assume separate cost buckets: input tokens, output tokens, and model inference CPU/GPU time. we typically provide per-token estimates for hosted and dedicated. example: on A100 class, non-quantized model might be $0.0009 per output token, quantized int8 variant $0.0004 — rough numbers until we run benchmarks.
[02:18] Diego: that gap is big, but what about batching? if we configure max batch 32 vs 8, how does cost shift?
[02:27] Priya: batching improves utilization — so unit token cost drops because more tokens amortize the kernel startup. but tail latency p99 will increase unless you use adaptive batching or small latency buckets for priority traffic. Redwood has per-route policies to limit batch wait time.
[02:46] Samir: can you quantify for our numbers? like with 40 QPS sustained and 150 output tokens average?
[02:53] Priya: rough calc: 40 qps * 150 = 6k output tokens/sec. with batch 16 on A100 you might need X concurrent workers; we'll put concrete numbers in the spreadsheet. expect per-output-token cost range $0.0003-$0.001 depending on model and quant. with KV cache at 30% reuse effective output tokens billed could drop ~30%.
[03:22] Jordan: also want to flag routing: we can route to cheaper quantized variants for non-critical requests and keep a high-quality model for priority routes. that often helps hit budget caps.
[03:35] Diego: security — if we go Private/VPC we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs, any SPOF in that flow?
[03:42] Priya: we support customer-managed KMS and HSM for encryption at rest, and audit logs — but the Private control plane differs slightly; we'll involve our security engineer. we can share SOC2 docs.
[03:58] Samir: good. benchmark plan?
[04:01] Priya: recommend 48-hour run with two phases: steady-state (24h) and spike testing (24h). run matrix with 3 model variants (base, quantized int8, and smaller fast model), two batch configs (8/32), and with/without KV caching. collect p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, GPU utilization, and token counts.
[04:29] Jordan: we'll provide a runbook and a benchmark spreadsheet with the assumptions (kernels, instance/region, tokenization differences). we usually link to a shared sheet — we'll include links in the follow-up.
[04:42] Lena: on infra, we prefer a VPC egress policy and can't open public endpoints. is the Private deployment necessary for the pilot or can we start hosted?
[04:54] Jordan: hosted is simplest to start; if you need VPC-only we can do a Private pilot but it adds on-boarding time ~2-3 weeks for networking and security review. hosted pilot can run in a week once we have sample traffic.
[05:11] Samir: timeline wise exec wants pilot results in 3 weeks; is that feasible?
[05:17] Priya: yes for hosted: day 0-2 ingest traffic and warm caches, day 3-5 run benchmarks, day 6 analyze and present. Private would push the schedule.
[05:29] Diego: budget cap is $15k for pilot, inclusive of runtime and Redwood support. can you model that?
[05:36] Jordan: absolutely — we'll run the cost model under that constraint and show recommended configuration to meet p99 and cost. we'll show tradeoffs: if cost exceeds cap we toggle batching, routing, or quantization.
[05:49] Samir: curious about tokenization differences across models — do you normalize to same token definitions?
[05:54] Priya: we normalize by token counts as our baseline, but note that different models have different tokenizers; we'll include tokenization correction factors in the sheet.
[06:05] Jordan: quick note: we may propose a small canary with 5% traffic to avoid large risk to production.
[06:12] Samir: makes sense. any benchmarking dependencies from our side?
[06:16] Priya: we need the 7-day sample trace, a representative set of prompts for eval, and an account/allowlist IP for the benchmark runner. also if you want to test Private we need VPC peering details.
[06:30] Lena: we'll get that.
[06:33] Jordan: a couple of numbers I'll call out in the follow-up: an initial hosted per-inference ballpark for your profile — using a medium open model quantized int8 + KV cache 30% reuse + batching 16, we estimate ~ $0.0012 per complete inference (input+output normalized). non-quantized could be up to $0.0024. these are placeholders.
[07:00] Diego: those are in range but still borderline with our $15k pilot, depends on traffic.
[07:06] Priya: we'll model two scenarios: optimistic (high cache reuse and good batching) and conservative (low cache reuse).
[07:12] Samir: what about throughput SLOs on Dedicated vs Hosted — is Dedicated significantly better p99?
[07:18] Priya: Dedicated buys predictability: reserved GPU pools reduce noisy neighbors and you can pick higher throughput hardware. latency can be lower more consistently; cost per token may be better at scale but has commit costs. we'll include a comparative sheet.
[07:35] Jordan: ok next steps recap — we'll send cost model + benchmark runbook, propose benchmark dates, Orion to share sample traffic and security constraints, schedule a 30-min follow-up to lock down the pilot window.
[07:50] Samir: thanks all.
[07:52] Diego: thanks
[07:53] Jordan: thanks, we'll follow up with links and the spreadsheet.
[07:58] (end recording)
